title: The Frog That Slipped
lines: Ravi was running down the path.
It was hot and the sun was up.
He had a net and a small jar.
Mom said, "Look at frogs, but let them go."
A frog was hopping in the wet mud.
Ravi stopped and grabbed at it.
The frog slipped from his hand.
He tripped and dropped his net.
Ravi sat still and stopped grabbing.
He held the jar down in the mud.
The frog went hopping right into it.
Ravi grinned. He had a frog!
Then he tipped the jar by the pool.
The frog went swimming off. Mom was glad.
"That was kind of you," she said.

questions.ask: What did Mom say Ravi had to do with the frogs?
questions.listenFor: Let them go. It is in the fourth line, inside the quote marks.

questions.ask: How did Ravi get the frog into the jar?
questions.listenFor: He sat still and held the jar down in the mud, and the frog hopped in.

questions.ask: Why do you think sitting still worked better than grabbing?
questions.listenFor: Any reason is fine. You want them to link the grabbing lines to the sitting still line.
